key_insight: Decouple “where to go” from “how far to go”: use a trusted first-order direction, then cheaply tune the step with zeroth-order function evaluations along that single direction.
engineering_relevance: This gives a lightweight, curvature-aware step-size strategy for LLM fine-tuning that can outperform fixed-step baselines without the cost of full line search.
method: First-order optimizer provides the descent direction.
Evaluate the objective at two additional points along that direction.
Fit a local 1D model to choose a bounded, near-optimal step size.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluations across multiple language-model and dataset settings, where ZFO often improved optimization and final performance over fixed-step first-order baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the local model choice and the method still relies on extra objective evaluations, so noisy or expensive function queries may limit practicality.
paper_title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
